body:
Brings the four Pass–shelat chapter 5–8 statement prongs and PAC support onto the campaign base, with topic/root exports, public reading interfaces and composition bridges. Designated security proofs remain admitted for external fills after the statement gates close.

Scope: authentication and hashing; OT/garbling/HBC secure computation; private-key CPA/CCA2 and public-key CPA games; sequential ZK and quantitative 3COL composition; extraction, learning and BPP bridges. The OT route retains canonical encryption, evaluator efficiency and enhanced-hard-core premises. This PR does not construct public-key CCA2 encryption.

Validation at `3f6db40e1688c4a0bb922c9575dd3bd2157a650b` (comparison ancestor `eee107e92a7db11f1f8c98a5c2867304f57ddc54`):

- Current source/object/direct-prerequisite reconciliation passes for all 467 union modules after 180+2 affected checks. Earlier unchanged objects are verified same-chat checks; this is not a second cold build. The root `TCSlib.lean` is export/byte pinned and was not elaborated.
- All61 changed Lean files have repository style comparison: ten inherited findings, zero new findings. Each complete new prong passes campaign checks in plain and check8b modes.
- Static repair/source and verification-tool reviews report 0 blockers/0 majors/0 minors. Five helper headers use equivalent full-domain Fin/coin transports; public hypotheses and algorithms are preserved apart from an equivalent decoder delegation to the shared API.
- Fresh collection for all 54 changed mathematical modules is running. Full current seals, all eleven controls, axiom/failure dispositions and external Gates 06A–D remain pending. Old-row diagnostic repair checks are explicitly not final coverage.

[Native reconciliation and evidence limits](https://github.com/Shilun-Allan-Li/tcslib/blob/b36ab1e2800788ab3167b65a6ce0a40e44f408ba/briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/maintainer/gate06-integration-2026-11-06/evidence-run/final-native-summary.json).

**Draft: not clear to merge.** The user dispatches the four selected Codex statement audits and merges only after their closure. S2 remains a separate PR #231 and separate acceptance record; this PR does not incorporate or attest that unmerged fill. The campaign target may advance through records-only commits; the checked comparison ancestor is stated above.

commits.messageBody:
… by canonical padding

Per the ruling of 2026-11-05, public-key games keep the fixed-length codec and
pad ciphertexts. padCt pads c to L(n) bits as <c, 1^k>; the padded decryptor
answers bottom on every non-canonical string (isPadded), since otherwise a
changed padding bit of the challenge would decrypt to the same message and
break CCA2. Padding is a bijection onto the canonical strings (pairFstD_padCt,
padCt_of_isPadded), so Dec* refusing the padded challenge is Dec* refusing the
challenge.

FixedLengthPKScheme with msgLen/ctLen; ofPadded builds one from any scheme and
an admissible bound L (correctness and lengths proved); PublicKeyScheme.padded
and BitPublicKeyScheme.padded for the ch. 2-4 schemes; exists_padBound proves a
bound always exists, from the machines' time bounds (runLenPoly).

The experiment Ind_b with Dec and Challenge oracles, the adversary run on pk
(toCompOn), and INDSecure: Definition 171.5. Sanity lemmas: CPA's Dec is
closed, CCA2's Dec refuses the challenge.

Claim 172.a: SingleBitSecure.padded_cpa stated (sorry under its sketch) and
tdpBitScheme_padded_cpa proved from it and Theorem 104.4.

TCSlib/Cryptography/Authentication/Lamport.lean: [PS10] Protocol 137.1 as a
SignatureScheme (n-bit messages, n^2-bit signatures) for a function family
f with n-bit inputs (lamportOWF) and an evaluator E agreeing with f on n-bit
inputs. Gen, Sign and Ver are instances of the ch. 2-4 block loop
(blockEncFun over the message bits, decListFun to flatten); all three are
proved polynomial-time, and correctness is proved (lamportVerFun_sign).

Ver tests the message and signature lengths before evaluating E, so E is only
ever run on n-bit preimage candidates. Without that test, an evaluator that is
admissible but misbehaves off its domain could make Ver accept forgeries that
do not invert f.

Theorem 137.2 (one-time security from a strong one-way function) is stated
under the source's sketch (plant y at a guessed (i, c), success eps/(2n)).
Compiles on the S2b olean tree; the only sorry is that theorem's body.

…d, its phase lemma proved

SequentialZK.lean: Protocol.seqRep pi Q runs pi Q(|x|) times with fresh coin
slices. Each phase has 2k moves: pi's k moves, then k filler moves of [].
The even phase length keeps the mover pattern of pi even when k is odd.
Parties recover the global move from their message count
(proverMoveIndex_exec, verifierMoveIndex_exec, proved). V_Q's verdict is the
conjunction of the phase verdicts; when the prover moves first it is also
V_Q's last (filler) message, per D8.

Proved: the position lemmas and seqRep_exec_phase (phase j of an honest
execution is an execution of pi with the coin slices j).

Stated under sketches (4 sorries): ZK.seqRep, StatZK.seqRep (error Q delta),
PerfectZKAbort.seqRep (statistical, error Q(n) 2^-n with n retries per phase),
InteractiveProof.seqRep. PerfectZK.seqRep is proved from StatZK.seqRep.

Two hypotheses found by adversarial instantiation:
- ProverBounded: under D8 a cheating V_Q may double its message lengths each
  phase; with a prover that echoes them (ZK for one run) and Q(n) = n, views
  grow like 2^Q, which no strict-PPT simulator matches. So the ZK statements
  assume the honest prover's messages have at most B(|x|) bits.
- 1 <= Q(n) for the interactive-proof statement (Q = 0 accepts everything).

R2-1 (major; also F5, F6): WeakLearnsUnder, WeakLearns and
not_weakLearnsUnder_of_predictAdv_le are described as accuracy/confidence
conditions at fixed parameters. They no longer attribute an
arbitrary-confidence requirement to [KV94, §4.1]: its weak learner need only
succeed with probability 1/q(n, size(c)) (p. 74), which is the confidence
δ = 1 − 1/q here, at the certified edge 1/p(n, size(c)) and a sufficient
sample count. A smaller δ is a stronger requirement for the same learner,
not a relaxation. Applying the bridge at a small δ, starting from that
definition, needs confidence amplification ([KV94, §4.2, pp. 76–77]), which
gives a different learner with its own sample count, running time and edge;
Prediction.lean's module docstring records this as layer 2's obligation.
The Defs "Unrestricted parameters" bullet and "Main definitions" line, the
PAC.lean contents line and the [KV94] references are aligned.

R2-2 (minor; F5, F11, Lean side): Prediction.lean's module docstring states
the bridge's condition γ + δ < γ' ≤ ½ and describes the expectation split
(error at most ε on the accuracy event, at most 1 on its complement of
probability at most δ). The design note and resolution record are outside
this branch.

R2-3 (minor; F14): Samples.lean cites the auditor-verified locations,
[SSBD14, §2.3.1] (product sampling) and [SSBD14, §3.1, Def 3.1] (i.i.d.
examples); the unchecked notation claim `S ~ D^m` is dropped.
